commit_message:
tests: add basic ECH tests

Test 4000 and 4001

Closes #17192

index e82fadd4a1..2c29015a87 100644
--- a/docs/ECH.md
+++ b/docs/ECH.md
@@ -474,5 +474,22 @@ to get the HTTPS RR and pass the ECHConfigList from that on the command line,
 if needed, or one can access the value from command line output in verbose more
 and then reuse that in another invocation.
 
 Both our OpenSSL fork and BoringSSL/AWS-LC have APIs for both controlling GREASE
 and accessing and logging ``retry_configs``, it seems wolfSSL has neither.
+
+### Testing ECH
+
+We have yet to add a robust test setup for ECH as that requires an ECH-enabled
+test server.
+
+We have added two basic tests though, aiming to ensure that the client sends a
+GREASE or real ECH extension when requested, and reacts correctly to the
+failure of ECH in the latter case. (Given that `stunnel` has no ECH support.)
+
+As with other similar tests, those tests require the `stunnel` tool be
+installed. On Ubuntu `sudo apt install stunnel4` achieves that.
+
+The test cases are:
+
+- data/test4000: GREASE ECH, expected result: connection succeeds
+- data/test4001: real ECH, connection fails with error 101 (ECH required)

+%if !wolfssl

+101
+%else
+35
+%endif
+%else
+35
+%endif
+</errorcode>
+</verify>
+</testcase>

fix_commit.message: rustls: apply memory function overrides, fixing an ECH buffer free
fix_commit.author: Viktor Szakats

findings.title: Raw free() on ECH buffer allocated by curl's overridable malloc, causing invalid free
findings.message: In init_config_builder_ech(), when an ECHConfig is supplied via the command line, the base64-decoded buffer `ech_config` is allocated by Curl_base64_decode() (curlx_base64_decode in later refactors), which performs its allocation through curl's internal, potentially-overridden malloc (curl_malloc / memory-tracking wrappers activated via curl_memory.h / memdebug.h when included by the allocating translation unit). In the cleanup path of init_config_builder_ech(), the buffer is released with a plain, unqualified `free(ech_config)` call. Because lib/vtls/rustls.c does not include "../curl_memory.h" / "../memdebug.h", this free() resolves to the plain libc free() instead of curl's matching deallocation function (Curl_cfree / memdebug free). When curl is built with memory-function overrides (curl_global_init_mem / CURLOPT allocator overrides) or with the debug memory tracker (CURLDEBUG/memdebug), the allocation and the free happen through mismatched allocator APIs. This causes an invalid free (reported by Valgrind and curl's own memory-tracking layer), and can lead to memory corruption or crashes/undefined behavior in builds that use custom allocators, since the pointer being freed was not actually obtained from the allocator that services the raw free() call.
findings.suggestion: Include "../curl_memory.h" and "../memdebug.h" (as the last includes) in lib/vtls/rustls.c so that malloc/calloc/realloc/free used throughout the file (including this free(ech_config) and the local cipher_suites malloc/free pair) resolve to curl's memory-tracked / overridable allocator wrappers, matching the allocator used by Curl_base64_decode(). This ensures the allocation and free are performed through the same allocator API, eliminating the invalid free detected by Valgrind and enabling correct behavior when memory-function overrides are supplied by the application.

ground_truth.root_cause: lib/vtls/rustls.c calls Curl_base64_decode() (which allocates through curl's internal, overridable malloc) to obtain the ECHConfig buffer but frees it with the plain libc free() because the translation unit never included curl_memory.h/memdebug.h, which are what redirect malloc/free calls in a given .c file to curl's tracked/overridable allocator functions. This mismatch between the allocator used to obtain memory and the deallocator used to release it is only safe by coincidence in default (no override, no memdebug) builds; it becomes an invalid free once curl's memory function overrides or memory debugging are engaged.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Raw free() on ECH buffer allocated by curl's overridable malloc, causing invalid free
